title: Nvidia pauses AI Compute Partnership over internal antitrust concerns
subtitle: Less than two months after launch, Nvidia halted the revenue-share program that gave the chip maker 50% of hourly rental income above cost — its own employees warned regulators would flag the arrangement.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Nvidia paused new deals under its AI Compute Partnership, less than two months after the program launched in July, according to reporting from The Wall Street Journal picked up by Reuters and Yahoo Finance. The initiative offered credit support to smaller cloud providers buying Nvidia chips in exchange for a share of revenue — specifically, Nvidia would take 50% of any hourly rental income above a base rate that covered the provider's costs. Employees inside Nvidia told current and prospective customers they were worried the structure could draw antitrust scrutiny given how much control it would give the chip maker over customer economics.

The pause is quieter than a formal cancellation but more consequential than it looks. Neocloud providers — CoreWeave, Nebius, Lambda, Crusoe, and roughly a dozen smaller players — have leaned on Nvidia's balance sheet to underwrite GPU purchases they cannot otherwise finance. Removing the revenue-share vehicle forces those providers to either raise more capital at higher cost or slow orders, which back-propagates into Nvidia's own bookings. The company said the broader July business model that opens compute access remains in place; the revenue-share sleeve does not.

The antitrust worry has a shape. When a dominant chip supplier both sells the hardware and captures upside on the workload rented on that hardware, competition regulators treat it as vertical foreclosure. The FTC and EU DG Comp have both been circling frontier-AI compute markets throughout 2026, and Nvidia's own employees flagging the risk internally is telling — it suggests the company would rather retreat than defend a case. Expect Nvidia to reappear with a restructured version that keeps the financing but drops the revenue split.

Takeaway for learners: 'AI infrastructure' economics run on unit-hour cost curves and financing terms as much as on chip performance. If you are building a business on rented GPUs, look at who is financing your cloud provider — a supplier discount that reappears as a revenue take-rate is not free capital. And when a vendor pulls a program on antitrust grounds, that is a leading indicator for how the market structure will settle over the next twelve months.
